correctness.rationale: For generic planes, section vertices are exactly crossed prism edges. The opposite-pair structure gives four base-edge intersections plus two for each subthreshold vertex pair, or n vertical edges when above all pair thresholds. The top two absolute projections on a fundamental azimuth sector are cos(phi) and cos(2pi/n-phi). Haar altitude is uniform, producing the exact elementary integral. Differentiating the arcsine expression gives a single interior critical point with derivative sign equal to 1-3cos^2(pi/n)z^2; endpoint probabilities are zero, so this is a strict unique maximum. Taylor expansion establishes the n^-2 asymptotic. An independent edge-crossing/azimuth-quadrature checker passed 2,850,000 section classifications across five even orders.

value.rationale: A natural maximal-section-complexity probability is determined exactly for a complete infinite even-sided prism family. The unique height optimizer and inverse-quadratic vanishing of the maximum are structural facts. The n=6 optimum is not the uniform prism, while the square optimum is cubic; this sharp nonuniformity and scaling are motivated by stereological interpretation, not arbitrary parameter substitutions.
